papers.title: Stress-controlled transfer of high-mobility organic semiconductor nanosheets for thin-film transistors
papers.summary: Organic thin-film transistors (TFTs) are key components for large-area and mechanically flexible electronic devices, and reliable fabrication methods beyond direct physical vapor deposition (PVD) are required, particularly for technical and non-planar surfaces. We fabricated organic TFTs by transferring organic small-molecule nanosheets. During the release and transfer process, the nanosheets experience significant mechanical stress, leading to plastic deformation or phase changes that can be quantified by X-ray diffraction (XRD). In accordance with classical bending theory, the mechanical stress can be significantly reduced by limiting the nanosheet thickness to 30 nm or less. Using this optimized thickness, we directly compare transferred nanosheets with thin films prepared by PVD on self-assembled monolayer (SAM)-functionalized bottom contacts. TFTs fabricated with transferred dinaphtho[2,3-b:2',3'-f]thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (DNTT) nanosheets exhibit a mobility of 0.32 cm2/V s and a subthreshold swing of 114 mV/dec, approaching state-of-the-art TFTs fabricated by direct PVD, which exhibit here a mobility of 0.42 cm2/V s. XRD indicates that transferred DNTT nanosheets exhibit superior crystalline order on the contacts compared to films grown by direct PVD. However, the PVD growth on the gate dielectric, i.e., on SAM-passivated Al2O3, is slightly better than on the sacrificial polymer layer. These results indicate that the transport properties of the transferred nanosheets are not primarily limited by the transfer process itself, but rather by the thin-film growth on the sacrificial water-soluble polymer layer. Transferable nanosheets have applications in hybrid devices and devices with unconventional geometries, e.g., non-planar transistors or devices containing free-standing thin films, where direct evaporation is challenging or not feasible.

papers.title: Competing hysteresis mechanisms in HZO/MoS2 transistors with a metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor gate stack
papers.summary: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors based on hafnium oxide offer a versatile platform for advanced memory concepts. Here, we demonstrate a proof-of-concept top-gated Hf0.5Zr0.5O2-based transistor integrating a metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor (MFMIS) gate stack with a two-dimensional MoS2 channel. The implementation of such an architecture is particularly challenging in MoS2, where the strong sensitivity of the channel to trapped charge can further complicate the balance between ferroelectric switching and charge redistribution within the MFMIS stack. By varying the MFM-to-MIS area ratio and the applied gate-voltage amplitude, we observe a systematic evolution of the transfer hysteresis consistent with competing ferroelectric polarization switching and trap-related contributions. Temperature-dependent measurements, zero-bias write/read experiments, and compact Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis modeling provide additional support for this interpretation. Despite the non-optimized gate stack, a substantial ferroelectric contribution to the device response is retained, while retention measurements reveal limitations associated with depolarization and trapping. These results demonstrate the feasibility of MFMIS ferroelectric transistors based on MoS2 and provide a basis for further optimization of their gate-stack design and memory performance.

papers.title: Wafer-scale synthesis of WSe <sub>2</sub> for high-performance p-type top-gated transistors and logic circuits
papers.summary: Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a promising pathway for next-generation electronics due to their exceptional electrical characteristics at atomically thin thickness. Nevertheless, the realization of high-quality p-type 2D-FETs remains a significant challenge for CMOS device integration due to surface damage and unintended n-doping induced during dielectric deposition. In this work, we report the wafer-scale synthesis of p-type WSe 2 films using metal-organic chemical vapor deposition and the fabrication of top-gate p-FETs through a buffer layer strategy, which provides superior electrostatic control and channel stability. The transistors exhibit excellent p-type performance, achieving a hole mobility of 10.49 ± 2.35 cm 2 V −1 s −1 with on/off current ratio exceeding 10 9 . By leveraging the process’s scalability, which ensures uniform and damage-free fabrication, we successfully produced reliable wafer-scale PMOS logic circuits. This study provides a scalable, damage-free integration solution for 2D electronics, paving the way for the practical realization of all 2D-based high-density electronics and circuits.

papers.title: Evolution mechanism of damage locations in drift region of SiC MOSFETs under heavy ion irradiation
papers.summary: This paper investigates the evolution mechanism of severe thermal damage locations in the drift region of the SiC MOSFETs under different applied drain voltages (VDS(irra)) during heavy ion irradiation using 587 MeV 36Kr ions. It is interesting to find from the post-irradiation blocking I–V curves that the drain–source leakage current increases significantly at about 500 V for the case under relatively low VDS(irra) (175–300 V) and increases rapidly at low voltage for the case under relatively high VDS(irra) (350 V). To explain this phenomenon, a local damage-related lifetime-model along the ion track is proposed and validated by technology computer-aided design simulations. The model indicates that thermal damage will develop near the p-base/n-drift junction once the damage near the n-drift/n-sub junction along the ion track becomes sufficiently serious with increasing VDS(irra). The proposed evolution mechanism of severe thermal damage locations can help analyze mechanisms of single-event leakage current and single-event burnout in SiC devices and guide radiation-hardening designs for SiC devices.

papers.title: High-mobility enhancement-mode thin-film transistors with 1.5 nm-thick ALD-grown Sn-doped In2O3 channels
papers.summary: Aggressive channel thickness scaling to the sub-2 nm regime is essential for strengthening electrostatic gate control in monolithic three-dimensional electronics, but it causes severe carrier depletion and transport degradation in In2O3 thin-film transistors (TFTs). Here, we demonstrate enhancement-mode TFTs with 1.5 nm-thick Sn-doped In2O3 (ITO) channels prepared by inhibitor-assisted atomic layer deposition. At the same physical channel thickness, the ITO TFT exhibits a field-effect mobility of 25.7 ± 1.4 cm2V−1s−1, a subthreshold swing of 129 ± 31 mV/dec, and a threshold voltage of 0.2 ± 0.2 V, whereas the undoped In2O3 TFT undergoes severe transport degradation. The ITO TFT also shows markedly improved positive-bias-stress stability, with a threshold voltage shift of 0.37 V after 3600 s, whereas the thickness-matched In2O3 TFT reaches 2.07 V within 1000 s and fails before 3600 s. Analysis of the effective mobility and sheet carrier density indicates that Sn doping mitigates carrier depletion in the sub-2 nm channel. The resulting carrier replenishment improves on-state transport and strengthens electrostatic screening against positive-bias-induced trap charging, thereby improving the mobility–positive-bias-stress stability balance. These results establish controlled Sn doping as an effective strategy for realizing high-mobility ultrathin In2O3 TFTs with positive-bias-stress stability for monolithic three-dimensional electronics.

papers.title: Cr2O3/β-Ga2O3 heterojunction diodes with orientation-dependent breakdown electric field
papers.summary: We report the fabrication of Cr2O3/β-Ga2O3 heterojunction diodes (HJDs) using reactive magnetron sputtering of Cr2O3 on highly doped β-Ga2O3 bulk substrates along (100), (010), (001), (110), and (011) orientation dependence of high electric field handling capability in β-Ga2O3. Additional relative permittivity values in (110) and (011) orientations of β-Ga2O3 were computed by using first-principles calculation methods for accurate apparent charge density (ND–NA) extraction and breakdown electric field analysis from capacitance–voltage measurements. The HJDs fabricated on n+ (110) exhibited breakdown electric fields >10 MV/cm up to 12.9 MV/cm, showing the highest experimentally observed parallel-plane junction electric field among β-Ga2O3-based junctions. Breakdown electric fields among (100), (010), (001), and (011) orientations showed distinct distribution in the range of 5.13–5.26, 5.10–7.05, 2.70–3.33, and 3.88–4.38 MV/cm, respectively, validating the orientational dependence of parallel-plane junction electric field at breakdown in low-symmetry monoclinic β-Ga2O3. The parallel-plane breakdown electric fields (EBr,ǁ) reported in this work were extracted when the device experienced breakdown at 100 mA/cm2 current density compliance, and should not be confused with critical electric field (Ec) as a function of drift layer doping concentration, which accounts for electric-field dependent impact ionization coefficients in Si, SiC, and GaN. This study can guide the choice of crystal orientation for high-performance gallium oxide-based devices that require high electric field handling capability.

papers.title: Hydration channel engineering in Tröger’s base-POP membranes for mono/multivalent cation and anion discrimination
papers.summary: Sustainable recovery of critical resources from complex aqueous streams is constrained by membranes that fail to combine rapid ion transport with precise mono/multivalent discrimination. Here, we report Tröger’s base-derived porous organic polymer (POP) membranes with rigid, covalently crosslinked microporous frameworks that stabilize angstrom-scale transport channels while suppressing hydration-induced swelling. These membranes render rapid monovalent-ion transport with near-complete exclusion of multivalent cations and anions, including Mg 2+ , Al 3+ , SO 4 2− , and PO 4 3− . Experiments and simulations show that steric confinement, dehydration penalties, and electrostatic interactions cooperatively raise migration barriers for multivalent ions in confined channels. The membranes achieve comprehensive mono/multivalent discrimination across both cationic and anionic systems. In multistage electrodialysis, they enable stage-amplified lithium enrichment from high-Mg brines with stable long-term operation and downstream recovery of crystalline Li 2 CO 3 . They also facilitate high-purity NaCl enrichment from simulated seawater. Overall, this platform offers a durable and energy-efficient route to selective resource recovery from complex aqueous streams.
